questions.question: What is a scale?
choices: An ordered set of pitches arranged by a pattern

questions.question: What is the tonic?
choices: The home or central pitch of a key

questions.question: How many different letter names appear in a major scale before the octave repeats?
What is the interval pattern of a major scale in whole and half steps?
What does a key signature help identify?
choices: The scale and tonal center a piece is organized around

questions.question: A piece has one sharp in its key signature. Which pitch is sharp?
What is a minor scale often associated with in introductory theory?
choices: A tempo that is always slow
A different interval pattern and tonal color from major
A piece played only by strings

questions.question: What is a chromatic scale?
choices: A scale using only white keys
A set of seven whole steps
A sequence moving by semitones through an octave

questions.question: How do relative major and minor keys relate?
choices: They share a key signature but have different tonics
They use identical melodies and tempos
They always have the same tonic

questions.question: Why practice scales with a metronome?
choices: To change the key signature automatically
To build even timing and coordination across pitches

questions.question: What is a whole step?
Which pair of natural notes is separated by a half step?
What does transposing a melody mean?
choices: Moving it to a different pitch level while preserving its relationships
Changing every rhythm but not pitches

questions.question: A melody sounds resolved when it ends on the tonic because the tonic acts as what?
choices: A tonal center or point of rest

questions.question: What is a pentatonic scale?
choices: A scale played only on piano
A scale with five pitches per octave

questions.question: How can accidentals affect a scale passage?
choices: They temporarily alter pitches from the key signature

questions.question: What is a key center?
choices: The pitch that feels most stable or at rest in a passage
The note printed in the page center
The loudest note in a chord

questions.question: A student confuses scale and key. Which distinction is accurate?
choices: A scale is a rhythm; a key is a tempo
A scale is an ordered pitch collection; a key organizes music around a tonal center
A scale names a clef; a key names a rest

questions.question: Why might a composer use a scale other than major or minor?
choices: To create a distinct melodic vocabulary or musical color

questions.question: If the tonic is D, what is the first scale degree?
